tldr: This paper generates a global 3D proxy (coarse 3D geometry) entirely from a single image and refines it with a video diffusion model, enabling scene video generation free of geometric collapses or accumulated drift even under rapid camera viewpoint changes.
hero_caption: Overall concept of SpatialCrafter. Given a single input image and an arbitrary camera trajectory, it first generates a global 3D proxy (a coarse 3D Gaussian representation) covering the entire scene all at once, and uses it as guidance to produce high-quality, geometrically consistent RGB-D video sequences.
overview:
For robots to act and plan in unknown environments, a "world model" that accurately imagines the surrounding 3D space is essential. Recently, there has been active work on exploring scenes from a single image using the powerful pretrained priors of video diffusion models (VDMs). However, because conventional VDMs lack explicit 3D structure, they suffer from geometric drift—such as walls warping during sharp turns or long-distance travel. Some methods reconstruct a 3D proxy (such as point clouds) from the input viewpoint to guide the generation. But because these proxies can only reconstruct what is already visible, the model repeatedly hallucinates ad-hoc geometry whenever the camera moves into occluded blind spots, leading to accumulating collapses.

The authors flipped the problem: if relying on reconstruction causes failure in unobserved areas, why not directly generate the entire scene's 3D structure from the very beginning? Their proposed framework, SpatialCrafter, uses a two-stage design. In the first stage, a generative model predicts a global 3D proxy (coarse 3D Gaussians) strictly aligned with the input image. In the second stage, a video diffusion model acts as a Generative Deferred Refiner, repainting and refining coarse RGB-D video rendered from this 3D geometry into photorealistic, high-detail footage.

To overcome the lack of large-scale 3D training data for this task, the authors also built a new hybrid dataset of 115K high-quality synthetic and real-world scenes. In experiments across synthetic and real-world benchmarks (RE10K, DL3DV), SpatialCrafter dramatically reduced loop-closing errors and geometric distortion even along long and loopy camera trajectories, setting a new state of the art.
contributions: Proposed the generative 3D proxy paradigm, predicting the entire scene's 3D structure from a single image all at once to fundamentally prevent hallucinations and accumulated drift in unobserved regions.

Developed the PaSS-Flow module to eliminate spatial misalignment between the input image and the generated 3D proxy, along with Parallel Geometry Injection and Proxy-Aware Corruption to inject coarse geometry without degrading the pretrained video model's generative capacity.
Constructed the first hybrid dataset (115K scenes) for single-image scene generation with accurate geometric annotations, integrating synthetic data and real-world videos.
Demonstrated state-of-the-art visual quality and consistent 3D geometry on synthetic and real benchmarks across challenging 81-frame sequences featuring rapid camera motions and loop trajectories.

sections.heading: Why do existing world models fail outside the field of view?
sections.summary: Video diffusion models (VDMs) are highly expressive world models, but maintaining explicit 3D consistency is difficult. Prior methods guided by partial 3D reconstructions hallucinate wildly in unobserved regions; this work proposes a two-stage approach built on a global 3D proxy that generates the entire scene upfront.
sections.details:
In robot navigation and embodied AI, building world models that enable agents to predict and reason about complex 3D environments is critical. Recently, video diffusion models (VDMs) pretrained on massive web video datasets have attracted wide interest, but stand-alone VDMs lack explicit 3D geometric constraints.

2D memory methods that cache past frames struggle with rapid camera rotations and occlusions, leading to unavoidable distortions. Conversely, 3D proxy approaches have emerged, reconstructing point clouds from the input image via monocular depth estimation to guide generation. However, they share a major flaw: they are merely reconstructive proxies showing surfaces visible from the input view. As the camera moves into occluded areas, the 3D guidance vanishes. The VDM is forced to fill gaps with stochastic guesses (hallucinations), causing the spatial structure to gradually collapse.

To solve this, the authors introduce SpatialCrafter. Rather than relying on partial reconstruction, they run a generative model that directly predicts the full scene's 3D structure upfront as a global 3D proxy. In the second stage, a VDM refines coarse footage rendered from this 3D proxy into clean, photorealistic video.

Making this work requires resolving the coordinate misalignment between the input image and the generated 3D proxy, as well as designing a refinement mechanism that does not overfit to coarse proxy noise. SpatialCrafter tackles both challenges head-on.

captions.F2: Comparison between conventional reconstructive proxies (Voyager) and the proposed generative proxy. On the left, the reconstructive proxy leaves unobserved areas as black missing regions when the viewpoint changes, causing severe geometric distortion and drift in the VDM output. On the right, the proposed method generates a global 3D proxy for the entire scene upfront, staying consistent under extreme viewpoint changes.

sections.heading: 2D memory vs. 3D proxies: Limits of prior work and where this paper stands
sections.summary: Camera-controllable video generation broadly splits into 2D memory approaches referencing past frames and 3D proxy approaches tracking point clouds. This work overcomes the limits of partial reconstruction and single-viewpoint panoramas by directly predicting the entire 3D scene.
sections.details:
Attempts to generate 3D scenes from images include NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) optimization, but these are computationally heavy on full scenes and often produce blurry textures.

Meanwhile, research leveraging video diffusion models (VDMs) has accelerated rapidly, falling into two main categories:

- 2D image memory methods (e.g., DFoT, WorldStereo): These keep previously generated frames in an external memory and reference them autoregressively. However, monocular depth errors accumulate over time, leading to scale drift and loop-closure failures when returning to previously visited locations.
- 3D proxy methods (e.g., ViewCrafter, Voyager): These use explicit point clouds as memory. Static variants leave occluded regions empty, while incremental variants that update the point cloud with newly generated frames suffer from error compounding—hallucinations from the VDM contaminate subsequent 3D proxies.
- Panorama proxies (e.g., Matrix-3D): These unroll a 360-degree panorama into a point cloud, but because it originates from a single optical center, it fundamentally cannot handle occlusions and parallax during large camera translations.

SpatialCrafter bypasses these iterative reconstruction traps by using a native 3D generative model to predict a global 3D representation of the entire scene before video generation even begins.

sections.heading: The foundation: TRELLIS and latent video diffusion models
sections.summary: The first stage is built upon TRELLIS, a 3D generative model using structured latent representations (SLAT), while the second stage is based on Wan 2.1, a state-of-the-art video foundation model. Both rely on Flow Matching to learn vector fields mapping noise to target distributions.
sections.details:
The framework builds on two core foundation models.

For the first stage of 3D proxy generation, it adopts the TRELLIS 3D generative framework. TRELLIS generates a sparse voxel field $\mathcal{P}=\{\mathbf{p}_i\}_{i=1}^{K}$ and predicts latent feature vectors $\mathbf{x}_i$ for each voxel to form a Structured LATent (SLAT) representation. This is decoded by a 3DGS decoder $\mathcal{D}_{\text{3D}}$ into a 3D Gaussian representation $\mathcal{X}$ that supports fast rendering. Training uses Conditional Flow Matching (CFM), learning straight-line probability paths from Gaussian noise to target states.

For the second stage of video refinement, the authors adopt the Wan 2.1 video diffusion foundation model. Input video is compressed by a causal VAE encoder $\mathcal{E}_{\text{vid}}$ into a 16-channel latent $\mathbf{z}$ downsampled $4\times$ temporally and $8\times$ spatially. Video generation follows the Flow Matching framework with a DiT architecture, updating latent variables conditioned on text $\mathbf{c}_{\text{txt}}$ and noise levels.

sections.heading: Inside the two-stage pipeline: 3D geometry prediction and deferred video rendering
sections.summary: SpatialCrafter uses point-cloud anchors to generate a globally aligned 3D proxy (PaSS-Flow) and refines its renderings via a video model (Generative Deferred Refiner). Training introduces corruption strategies (PAC) to build robustness against proxy flaws, supported by a newly created 115K-scene dataset.
sections.details:
The system takes a single reference image $\mathbf{I}_0$ and a camera trajectory $\mathcal{T}$ as input, producing a spatio-temporally consistent RGB-D video sequence. It consists of three key components:

4.1 Global 3D Proxy Generation (PaSS-Flow)
The primary challenge in single-image 3D generation is spatial misalignment between the generated 3D space and the input image camera frame. Any shift causes severe ghosting in downstream video models. The authors propose the Point-anchored Sparse Structure Flow (PaSS-Flow) module. A partial point cloud derived from the input image and its estimated depth is voxelized and fed into a DiT as explicit geometric anchors $\mathcal{V}_{\text{cond}}$. This reframes unconditional generation into an anchor-constrained 3D completion task, producing a global 3D proxy strictly aligned with the input image.

4.2 Generative Deferred Refiner
A coarse RGB-D video sequence is rendered from the coarse 3D proxy along the target trajectory. Analogous to deferred shading in graphics, the video foundation model paints in high-frequency textures and fixes geometric flaws. Two key techniques make this work:
- Parallel Geometry Injection: Coarse RGB and depth latents are concatenated horizontally into $\mathbf{z}_{\text{geo}}$ and channel-concatenated with the pretrained VDM latents. The pretrained weights remain frozen while only LoRA parameters inside the DiT are fine-tuned, injecting geometric guidance without degrading photorealistic generative capacity.
- Proxy-Aware Corruption (PAC): The generated 3D proxy inevitably exhibits artifacts like blur and missing holes. During training, perturbations such as Gaussian blur, block noise, and partial depth dropouts are applied stochastically to the coarse RGB-D renders. This teaches the model when to adhere to underlying geometry and when to autonomously inpaint missing regions.

4.3 Large-Scale Hybrid Data Engine
The dataset combines indoor synthetic panoramas (SpatialGen) and real-world videos (RealEstate10K, DL3DV). For real videos, consistent depth was estimated using ViPE and DAv3 to reconstruct high-quality point clouds. Low-quality reconstructions were strictly filtered out, resulting in 115,295 3D scene generation pairs and 87,115 video generation pairs.

captions.F3: Overall pipeline of SpatialCrafter. Top: The 3D proxy generation stage uses point anchors (PaSS) from the input image to generate coarse 3D Gaussians. Bottom: Coarse RGB-D video is rendered along the target trajectory, perturbed with PAC, and passed through a video DiT with LoRA to produce high-fidelity RGB-D video.
captions.F5: Data curation pipeline for the 115K-scene hybrid dataset. Consistent geometry is extracted from synthetic data (SpatialGen) and real-world videos (DL3DV, RE10K) to generate paired coarse 3D Gaussians, high-quality videos, and text captions.

sections.heading: Unmatched 3D consistency across long 81-frame trajectories
sections.summary: Evaluations on synthetic and real benchmarks tested challenging, long 81-frame camera paths. SpatialCrafter outperformed existing methods across all visual quality (FVD, PSNR) and geometric consistency metrics (RPE, RVE), with ablation studies confirming the role of each module.
sections.details:
Experiments were conducted on the synthetic SpatialGen-Video benchmark (104 scenes with loop trajectories) and real-world RE10K and DL3DV datasets. All methods received identical input images and camera trajectories to generate long 81-frame videos.

Baselines included 2D memory approaches (DFoT, GeometryForcing) and reconstructive 3D proxy methods (ViewCrafter, GEN3C, Voyager). To separate the impact of the dataset from architectural advantages, the authors also trained a baseline called Voyager † using their new dataset.

In quantitative evaluations (Table 1), SpatialCrafter achieved the top results across all benchmarks:
- On SpatialGen-Video, it achieved an FVD of 193.54 (runner-up: Voyager † at 232.88) and an RPE of 0.093 (runner-up: Voyager † at 0.125).
- On RE10K, it recorded an FVD of 148.71 and a PSNR of 17.185.
- Crucially, comparing against Voyager † showed that while retrained on higher-quality data, Voyager † still lagged far behind SpatialCrafter in geometric metrics (RPE, RVE). This proves the performance jump stems from the global generative proxy design rather than data alone.

Qualitative results (Figure 7, left) showed that under rapid turns, existing methods dropped walls or froze into static images, whereas SpatialCrafter rendered distant outdoor buildings and interior depths with continuous consistency.

Ablation studies (Table 2, Figure 7, right) highlighted several findings:
- Removing PaSS-Flow caused coordinate misalignment with the input view and severe distortion (Figure 4).
- Conditioning only on camera trajectory parameters led to drift over long distances (Figure 7a).
- Removing depth (RGB-only) caused inconsistencies in unobserved regions (Figure 7b).
- Removing PAC caused the model to replicate unobserved black holes from the proxy directly into the output (Figure 7c). Adding PAC gave the network the robustness to naturally inpaint those voids.

captions.F7: Left: Comparisons with existing methods. Under extreme viewpoint changes, prior methods collapse (Voyager) or freeze (GeometryForcing), while the proposed method (Ours) tracks consistently without artifacts. Right: Ablation studies showing the advantages of the full model over (a) camera-only, (b) RGB-only, and (c) without PAC (where black missing holes persist).

sections.heading: Conclusion and what lies ahead
sections.summary: SpatialCrafter combines global 3D proxy generation with video diffusion refinement for single-image scene exploration. By effectively eliminating geometric collapse and cumulative drift, it establishes a solid foundation for robotics and world modeling research.
sections.details:
This paper presented SpatialCrafter, a novel two-stage framework for generating explorable 3D scene videos from a single image. It addresses the fundamental flaw of previous video world models—hallucination and geometric drift caused by reliance on partial reconstructions—by generating a complete global 3D proxy first and refining it with a video diffusion model.

Key technical contributions include PaSS-Flow for strict spatial alignment with the input image, Parallel Geometry Injection to preserve pretrained video knowledge, and Proxy-Aware Corruption to handle proxy flaws. Additionally, the curation and release of a 115K-scene hybrid dataset represents a major resource for the community.

By maintaining geometric consistency through wide camera swings and long loop trajectories, this approach represents a promising step forward for robot self-localization, simulation environment generation, and planning world models.

takeaways: Shifting from reconstruction to generation: Relying on sequential reconstruction of partial point clouds inevitably fails in occluded blind spots; predicting the 3D proxy with a generative model is critical for long-range scene exploration.

Spatial alignment via anchor constraints: Coordinate misalignment common in 3D generative models is effectively solved by conditioning the model on unprojected partial point clouds as geometric anchors.

Training for imperfection (PAC): Deliberately injecting noise, blur, and missing patches into coarse proxies during downstream video model training teaches the model to self-heal and inpaint proxy artifacts during inference.
limitations: Two-stage computational cost: Running sequential 3D proxy generation followed by video DiT refinement requires further speedups to support real-time, online control on physical robots.

Scalability to massive, complex scenes: Because the approach relies on the resolution capacity of global 3D proxies (voxels/3DGS), scaling to sprawling multi-room environments may face memory constraints and representation limits.
